context: The agent reads a git diff introducing a new user-facing search feature for user profiles and writes a commit message to commit-message.txt. The criteria verify that the commit subject line follows conventional commit formatting rules: correct type classification, proper prefix format, length limit, lowercase, no trailing punctuation, and active voice.

checklist.name: Standard type keyword
checklist.description: The subject line in commit-message.txt begins with a recognized conventional commit type keyword: one of feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, ci, perf, build, or test

checklist.name: Correct type: feat
checklist.description: The type used is `feat` — the staged changes introduce new user-facing search functionality, which is a feature addition, not a fix, refactor, or other type

checklist.name: Type opens the subject line
checklist.description: The type keyword appears at the very start of the subject line, with nothing before it (no leading spaces, dashes, or other characters)

checklist.name: Colon follows type
checklist.description: The type keyword is immediately followed by a colon with no space between the type and the colon (e.g., `feat:` not `feat :` or `feat -`)

checklist.name: Subject within 50 characters
checklist.description: The entire subject line (first line of commit-message.txt), including the type prefix and colon, is 50 characters or fewer in total length

checklist.name: Type prefix in lowercase
checklist.description: The type keyword itself is lowercase (e.g., `feat:` not `Feat:` or `FEAT:`)

checklist.name: Description in lowercase
checklist.description: The text following the colon in the subject line uses lowercase letters — no mid-sentence capitalization or title-cased words (acronyms excepted)

checklist.name: No trailing punctuation
checklist.description: The final character of the subject line is not a period (`.`), exclamation mark (`!`), question mark (`?`), comma (`,`), or semicolon (`;`)

checklist.name: Active voice
checklist.description: The subject line description uses active voice (e.g., 'adds search to user profiles', 'introduces profile search endpoint') — not passive constructions such as 'search was added', 'profile search is introduced', or 'search functionality has been implemented'

checklist.name: Commit as implied subject
checklist.description: The description after the colon is phrased with the commit as the implied subject — it reads as an action the commit performs (e.g., 'adds…', 'introduces…', 'enables…') rather than a noun phrase or a sentence with an explicit external subject

checklist.name: Flags migrations
checklist.description: If the diff includes a database migration, the body explicitly flags it
